Nora (People Ops): Heads up 11 Ib4m returning from parental leave in two weeks and planning to travel for a short family trip during week 2. Want to confirm how travel affects phased-return scheduling and paperwork.
Ben (Engineering Manager): Congrats! Travel is fine. Just mark the dates on your phased-return form and note the reduced availability. If you need asynchronous coverage, flag meetings and I'll reassign.
Nora (People Ops): Do we have to submit travel receipts or any extra docs for intermittent leave? It's mostly regular hours but with two 3-hr pickup windows and one travel day.
Sam (Payroll): Travel itself doesn't change leave docs. For intermittent parental leave, upload birth/adoption docs as usual. Intermittent windows are set in the portal; payroll treats travel day as worked if you log hours unless you request it as unpaid leave.
Nora (People Ops): Where to upload the leave addendum for travel?
DocsBot: Upload forms at https://hr.redwood-inference/internal/leave -> Parental / Intermittent. Accepted: .pdf, .png, .jpg. Receipt confirmation email within 24 hours.
Nora (People Ops): IT 11 need a hotspot for the trip days and a short-term loaner for a second monitor when I'm back on campus. What's the process?
IT Team: Submit an equipment loan request with exact loan dates and shipping address. Standard loaner period is 6 weeks; hotspot requests usually approved for travel days.
Ben (Engineering Manager): @Nora also include a 1-page async plan: which PRs to ignore, who to ping for approvals, and preferred overlap hours. That makes coverage easier.
Nora (People Ops): Will do. Quick payroll Q: if I elect the company top-up for the intermittent windows, does that apply pro rata to travel day if I work partial hours?
Sam (Payroll): Top-up applies to approved intermittent leave hours only. If you record partial worked hours on travel day, top-up will prorate for the approved leave portion. DM me and I can run an example calc for your dates.
Nora (People Ops): Thanks! I'll upload the travel note and handover doc today and ping Sam for the payroll example. :heart:
